breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for a dry sky to start. Fierce calm is Thursday composure under showers: charge first, body second, two clean must-dos, quiet admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Thursday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Rain outside; tempo inside. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Gnostic texts rarely reward the one who waits for perfect weather. They reward the one who recognizes the door while standing in the rain. Thursday’s showers are not delay — they are veil practice. Cross the threshold with breath and body before you ask the day for clarity.
Hermetic operators treat gray mornings as fuel, not omen. What is veiled is still active. Keep the competitive calm: act from the current you already carry, not the clearance the weather withholds.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.body: Solomon’s wisdom was not speed for its own sake — it was right proportion. A king who rushes judgment breaks the vessel he meant to fill. Your morning is that vessel: breath sets the measure, body fills it, then the desks get a hearing. A day measured before it is opened holds shape; a day opened first spills.
grimoire.practice: After four rounds of box breathing, name one must-do out loud. Then start the 3-minute opener. Do not open mail until both are done.

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — Scan with VirusTotal, Shield with 10MinuteMail, Capture with Scribe

lesson.oneLiner: Three legal tools, one habit: scan before you open, shield throwaway signups, capture the SOP once.
beats: Scan — VirusTotal runs a file or URL across 70+ engines before you click.
Shield — 10MinuteMail (or similar) for one-off accounts so spam never hits your real inbox.
Capture — Scribe records a workflow once into a shareable SOP your future self (or agent) can rerun.
Rule: do not bookmark fifty tools — install the habit that uses three.
lesson.takeaway: Operator hygiene compounds. @mmmik000: scan → shield → capture. Then get back to the board.
